gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker 140W 4-Port (A2697), ChatGPT's pick in both chats, drops its MacBook port to 100 W, below Apple's 140 W fast-charge line, as soon as a second device goes into the C3 or USB-A port, and to 70 W when C1 and C2 are both in use. Both figures come from Anker's own US output table.
standout_why: I compared against thegadgetmasters.com, cited in chat 1 and updated 2026-11-23. It gives no prices and no split figures for any charger, and says only that single-port power does not guarantee 140 W when other devices are plugged in. I also compared against macworld.com, cited in chat 2 and updated 2026-11-25. For the A2697 it prints only the four-device split (65+45+12+12 W) and '134W with four devices'. It never says the 140 W port falls to 100 W with just one extra device. ChatGPT's own answer said only that connecting other devices 'reduces the power' and gave no number. Apple's support page sets the 140 W line but names no third-party charger.
decides: This weakens ChatGPT's top pick for anyone who charges a phone from the same brick. With any second device plugged in, the A2697 is a 100 W charger as far as a 16-inch MacBook Pro is concerned. The pick moves toward a single-port 140 W adapter (Apple, Plugable) or a 160 W multi-port. For the 160 W multi-ports, Anker (Prime 160W) and UGREEN (Nexode Pro 160W) print a 160 W two-port total but no per-port split, so the page must not claim they keep 140 W. Either way it should state the cable rule: MagSafe 3, or a 240 W USB-C cable on Nov 2023 and later models. That rule favors bundles that include a 240 W cable, such as UGREEN's own Nexode Pro 160W + 240W cable at $61.98.
